sentences.text: Hello and welcome to the Slow English Podcast.
My name is Emili.
I am happy you are here.
Today we will talk about Ivory Coast.
The country is also called Cote d'Ivoire in French.
It is a country in West Africa.
Let's learn about it in slow and simple English.
Are you ready?
Let's begin.
Where is Ivory Coast?
Ivory Coast is in West Africa.
It is next to the Atlantic Ocean.
It shares borders with Liberia, Guinea, Mali, Burkina Faso and Ghana.
It has beautiful beaches, forests and cities.
What is the capital city of Ivory Coast?
The official capital is Yamosukro, but the biggest city is Abidjan.
Abidjan is a modern and busy city.
It has tall buildings, markets, schools and music.
Yamosukro is known for the basilica of Our Lady of Peace, a very large church.
How many people live in Ivory Coast?
About 30 million people live in Ivory Coast.
Many people live in Abidjan and other cities.
Others live in villages and farming areas.
There are more than 60 ethnic groups in the country.
It is a very diverse nation.
What language do people speak in Ivory Coast?
The official language is French.
Many people speak French in school, at work and in the government.
But people also speak many local African languages, such as Baule, Dula Sonufa.
Many people speak two or three languages every day.
What is the weather like in Ivory Coast?
The weather is hot and humid.
There are two seasons.
Rainy season with heavy rain from May to October.
Dry season with little rain from November to April.
The country is green and tropical in the south and drier in the north.
What does Ivory Coast look like?
Ivory Coast has many different landscapes, beaches along the ocean,
rainforests in the south, savannas in the north, mountains in the west.
There are also rivers, lakes and national parks.
Nature is important in Cote d'Ivoire.
What animals live in Ivory Coast?
The country is home to many wild animals, such as elephants, monkeys, antelopes,
leopards, crocodiles, birds and butterflies.
In Thai National Park, you can see animals in the rainforest.
There are also farms with goats, chickens and cows.
What do people eat in Ivory Coast?
People eat rice, cassava, yam, plantains and maize.
They also eat fish, chicken and vegetables.
Popular dishes include attieke made from cassava like couscous,
alaco, fried plantains, kajunous, spicy stew with chicken and vegetables.
Food too, mashed yam or plantain eaten with soup.
For dessert, people eat fruit, cakes or peanuts.
They drink bisap, hibiscus juice, ginger juice and coffee or tea.
What is life like in Ivory Coast?
Life is different in the cities and in the villages.
In cities, people work in offices, shops or schools.
In villages, many people are farmers or crafts people.
Family is very important.
People often live with their parents, grandparents and children.
Music and dance are part of everyday life.
People enjoy coupé de calle music and traditional drumming.
What are some holidays and traditions in Ivory Coast?
Independence Day is on August 7 with parades in music.
Eat and Christmas are both celebrated.
People also enjoy New Year's Day with fireworks and parties.
Each ethnic group has its own festivals with dancing, food and special clothes.
Some fun facts about Ivory Coast.
The name Ivory Coast comes from the past trade of elephant ivory.
The flag is orange, white and green.
Similar to Ireland but reversed.
Ivory Coast is one of the world's biggest producers of cocoa, used to make chocolate.
The country also exports coffee, cotton and cashew nuts.
Zuglu and coupé de calle are popular music styles from Cote d'Ivoire.
Now you know many things about Ivory Coast.
You know where it is, what people speak and what they eat.
You learned about the animals, music, food and daily life.
Great work!
I am Emili.
Goodbye or as they say in French, all of war.
